{{Short description|Italian physicist}}
'''Franco Cacialli''' is an Italian physicist affiliated with the [[University College London]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Franco Cacialli |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/physics-astronomy/people/professor-franco-cacialli |website=UCL Department of Physics and Astronomy |publisher=[[University College London]] |accessdate=29 November 2019 |language=en |date=25 April 2018}}</ref> He was awarded the status of Fellow in the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> after he was nominated by the Division of [[Materials physics|Materials Physics]] in 2009,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2009&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellows 2009|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> for "his significant contributions to the science and technology of [[organic semiconductor]]s and related applications, and especially for seminal contributions to the scanning near-field optical microscopy (SNOM) assisted [[lithography]] of organic semiconductor nanostructures.

Cacialli is a co-director of the London Institute for Advanced Light Technologies<ref>{{cite web |title=Directors |url=https://london-light.org/people/|website=London Institute for Advanced Light Technologies |accessdate=29 March 2021}}</ref>
